about: A server that puts many free AI model providers behind one OpenAI-style endpoint, with routing and automatic failover.

prs.title: Two tool calls at once from Gemini stay two calls
prs.broken: When Gemini asked to run two tools at once in a streamed reply, the server glued them into one broken call. Most clients then got an error, and the key was put on a cooldown.
prs.changed: Each streamed tool call now gets its own number, like the other providers already did, and calls without an id no longer share one.
prs.matters: Agents that run tools in parallel through Gemini work instead of failing.

prs.title: A cut-off answer is marked incomplete
prs.broken: When a model stopped because it hit its length limit or a content filter, the Responses endpoint still called the answer completed.
prs.changed: Such a turn is now marked incomplete with the reason, the way the Responses API defines it, both streamed and not.
prs.matters: Coding tools can tell a cut-off answer from a finished one instead of taking half an answer as the whole.

prs.title: Streamed replies report the real token counts
prs.broken: When a reply was streamed, the provider's real token counts were thrown away and a rough guess was reported instead.
prs.changed: The real counts from the provider are now kept and passed on at the end of the stream.
prs.matters: Usage logs, dashboards and per-key limits are accurate for streaming tools, which is most of the traffic.

prs.title: The one-tool-at-a-time setting is passed on to the model
prs.broken: A request asking the model to call at most one tool per turn lost that setting, so the model could still call several.
prs.changed: The setting is now read and sent to the provider as its own one-call-at-a-time option.
prs.matters: Apps that need tools run one by one get the behavior they asked for.

prs.title: Tool calls stay in the same turn as the text before them
prs.broken: In two kinds of replayed conversations, tool calls were split into a second assistant turn, which some providers reject.
prs.changed: Tool calls are now joined to the assistant turn just before them when that turn has none yet.
prs.matters: Conversations that mix search or reasoning with tool calls work with more providers.

prs.title: Cached prompt tokens are reported instead of zero
prs.broken: The responses endpoint always said zero prompt tokens came from the cache, even when the provider said many did.
prs.changed: The provider's cached token count is now passed through in the usage numbers.
prs.matters: People can see how much prompt caching is saving them.
